long_biography.plain_text:
Steel businessman Alonso Ancira first worked underground as a teenager. After he failed school subjects, his father sent him to the family's copper mine in Michoacán, where he spent eight months assisting drillers. He later recalled that experience when discussing the working conditions of miners.

His industrial plans sought to reduce dependence on standard commercial steel. At AHMSA, he signed an equipment agreement with Primetals Technologies to support higher-value products for automotive, energy and specialised industrial customers. The programme included thinner rolled sheet and additional cold-rolling capacity, aiming to supply grades that Mexican buyers had previously imported.

Steel businessman Alonso Ancira first worked underground as a teenager. After he failed school subjects, his father sent him to the family's copper mine in Michoacán, where he spent eight months assisting drillers. He later recalled that experience when discussing the working conditions of miners.

His industrial plans sought to reduce dependence on standard commercial steel. At AHMSA, he signed an equipment agreement with Primetals Technologies to support higher-value products for automotive, energy and specialised industrial customers. The programme included thinner rolled sheet and additional cold-rolling capacity, aiming to supply grades that Mexican buyers had previously imported.
